description: B7'S GABLES FRAMED AND SHEATHED (GABLE-END-STUDS; docs/reference-parts/buildings.md B7, docs/BACKLOG.md GABLE-END-STUDS, Chief Architect's Build Framing): b7-ceiling-joists' tree (B7's 288 x 192 outline sketch, loft.floor 1.2.0, loft.wall 1.3.0 on the floor, the door and four windows at 1.1.0) with its roof at loft.roof 1.7.0, every default kept: 1.6.0's gable, notches and 11 ceiling joists, then Gable ends 'Studs and sheathing': on each end wall's top plate a 2x6 SPF gable stud at each of the wall's 11 inner layout centres, cut on the slope to the rafters' underside (long point up), and the wall's 7/16 OSB carried up in its own columns and corner rips to the rafters' top plane. model.json is EXACTLY the sketch and the expansions with their member materials; members.json is each body's member metadata with its plugin (packages/loft-plugins/tests/test_gable_end_studs.py pins both; services/geometry/tests/test_gable_ends_b7.py checks the STEP, interference, the cut list, the mass and the 28 ft, 8/12, B10, 291, 171-span and turned cases).
derivation: INDEPENDENT of the plugins: services/geometry/tests/test_gable_ends_b7.py adds 22 studs and 12 panels typed from buildings.md to test_ceiling_joists_b7.house() (B7's independent build123d script with its joists, 228 solids). Studs: the (Y, Z) quad (c - 0.75, P), (c + 0.75, P), (c + 0.75, U(c + 0.75)), (c - 0.75, U(c - 0.75)) at P = 108.59375 and U(y) = 106.1770833 + min(y, 192 - y) / 2, extruded X 0..5.5 for c = 21.5 + 16k (the left wall lays out from its start at the front, Y 5.5) and X 282.5..288 for c = 170.5 - 16k (the right wall runs clockwise from the back, Y 186.5), k = 0..10. OSB: the (Y, Z) polygon from the plate up to the top plane U(y) + 7.25 sqrt(1.25), peaked at Y 96, extruded X -7/16..0 and 288..288 7/16, in the walls' columns (left Y -7/16, 5.5, 53.5, 101.5, 149.5, 186.5, 192 7/16; right Y -7/16, 5.5, 42.5, 90.5, 138.5, 186.5, 192 7/16). The STEP matches the 262 solids solid for solid (volume to 1e-4 in^3, bounds to 1e-5 in).

long points: d / 2 - 29/12 at each stud's higher face, d from the nearer eave wall's outside face (22.25, 38.25, 54.25, 70.25, 86.25 and 91.25, 75.25, 59.25, 43.25, 27.25, 11.25): 262.791667 in a gable, both gables alike (mirror layouts). A stud is 5.5 x 1.5 x (long - 0.375): 8.25 x (262.791667 - 4.125) = 2 134 in^3 a gable, 4 268 for both.

OSB: Y -7/16 .. 192 7/16 between the plate and the top plane, k = 114.282829 - 108.59375 = 5.689079 at Y 0: 2 x (k x 96.4375 + ((96^2 - (7/16)^2) / 2) / 2) = 5 705.185554 in^2 a gable, x 7/16 = 2 496.018680 in^3; 4 992.037360 for both. (The PM's 4 155.68 in^2 stops at the underside plane and leaves the end rafters' outside faces bare: RESEARCH section 23, GABLE-END-STUDS.)
surface_area, centroid, mass_g and center_of_mass are the script's solids summed (expected_numbers()): spf_lumber 450, southern_pine_pt 582, osb 641 and plywood 577 kg/m^3.
bounding_box: b7-ceiling-joists' but its top, the gable OSB's peak 114.282829 + 48 = 162.282829 in (the ridge board's top is 161.907829).

topology and MESH from the script's B-rep: b7-ceiling-joists' 1 608 faces, 3 456 edges and 228 shells plus 22 studs and 10 panels of 6 faces and 12 edges and 2 peak panels of 7 faces and 15 edges: 1 814 faces, 3 870 edges, 262 shells; every face is planar, so a face of n edge-vertices meshes as n - 2 triangles on n vertices: 6 912 + 32 x 24 + 2 x 30 = 7 740 vertices and 3 696 + 32 x 12 + 2 x 16 = 4 112 triangles. The kernel's build of model.json meets every count exactly.

Interference none (test_nothing_interferes probes every pair whose boxes overlap, exactly): each stud stands on its wall's top plate and its cut top meets the gable-end rafter's underside face to face; the OSB stands on the wall's OSB and lies outside the framing, on the end rafter's outside face.
tolerance_rationale: Measured first, then set (geometry-gates skill). The bounds are ABSOLUTE and the part is ~4.9e9 mm^3 summed over 262 bodies, so the double-precision sum carries round-off of a few ULPs of the sum (~9.5e-7 each): the kernel differs from the script by +6.7e-06 mm^3 on the volume, -3.0e-07 mm^2 on the area, <= 1.9e-12 mm on the centroid, <= 5.5e-12 mm on the centre of mass, 9.3e-10 g on the mass and 0 on the bounds; summing the kernel's own 262 solid volumes in 200 shuffled orders spreads -1.9e-06 .. +7.6e-06 mm^3 about the analytic volume, so the volume's 6.7e-6 is summation order, not geometry (b7-ceiling-joists' class). 2e-5 is 2.6x the worst order and ~4e-15 relative; one gable stud missed takes at least 8.25 x 2.833 x 16 387 = 383 000 mm^3 and a stud cut 1e-3 in off its plane ~135 mm^3, so either fails by seven orders or more.
roundtrip_tolerance_rationale: KERNEL-LEVEL, b7-outline's class, measured 2026-10-29: OCCT's STEP writer rounds the sloped rafters', the notched OSB panels', the snipped joists' and the 22 sloped gable studs' and 12 gable panels' irrational coordinates. Round-trip drift: volume -2.67e-4 mm^3, area -2.31e-5 mm^2, centroid <= 9.9e-11 mm (plugin); the independent build123d twin (test_gable_ends_b7.house(), exported with build123d's export_step) drifts -3.30e-4 / -2.30e-5, so it is OCCT's STEP, not Loft's export. 1e-3 is 3.0x the worst and the b2-roof goldens' bound; it applies to volume and area only, the centroid and bounds keep ROUNDTRIP_TOL.
